questions.prompt: In a patient with dyspnea and a low clinical probability of pulmonary embolism, which fibrin-breakdown marker can help exclude venous thromboembolism when negative in an appropriate diagnostic pathway?
questions.note: D-dimer measures breakdown products of cross-linked fibrin. A negative result can help exclude thromboembolism in appropriately selected patients; a positive result is nonspecific. BNP instead reflects cardiac wall stress and supports heart-failure assessment. The original stem did not distinguish these roles, so the intended clot-related role is now explicit.
